title: Retiming Robot Demonstrations with a Learned Speed Prior
abstract: arXiv:2610.32676v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The pace of a robot demonstration is often determined by the teleoperator rather than by the task itself. As a result, the same motion can appear at widely different speeds across demonstrations, and policies trained on such data may inherit operator-specific timing along with task behavior. We propose to learn a speed prior directly from large-scale demonstration data. Given a task instruction, a motion path and the images along it, it predicts a distribution over execution speed along the path, from which a chosen quantile defines a consistent clock for retiming each demonstration. Existing methods derive the acceleration signal from the very data they accelerate, so each new task costs another fit, annotation, or pair of predefined rates. translated_title: 基于习得速度先验的机器人演示重定时
translated_abstract: 机器人演示的节奏往往由远程操作者而非任务本身决定。因此，同一动作在不同演示中可能以差异悬殊的速度出现，而在此类数据上训练的策略可能会连同任务行为一起继承操作者特有的时间节奏。我们提出直接从大规模演示数据中学习一个速度先验。给定任务指令、运动路径以及沿路径的图像，该先验预测沿路径执行速度的分布，从中选定一个分位数即可定义一个一致的时钟，用于对每条演示进行重定时。现有方法从其要加速的数据本身中提取加速信号，因此每个新任务都需要额外的拟合、标注或一对预定义的速度；而一个训练好的速度先验则可覆盖语料库中的所有任务。我们在机器人远程操作数据以及手持式演示（即由人类手臂而非机器人手臂执行动作的演示）上拟合了速度先验……
tldr: 提出从大规模演示数据中学习一个速度先验，为任意任务预测执行速度分布并生成一致的时钟来重定时演示，从而消除操作者个人节奏对策略训练的干扰。
en_tdlr: We learn a speed prior from large-scale demonstration data that predicts a distribution over execution speeds for any task, providing a consistent clock to retime demonstrations and remove operator-specific timing biases from policy training.
